# You're inside a real Advisor Prep Hero workspace

This is running in your browser. No install, no account, nothing saved to a server. It's a pretend client matter for a CPA, pre-loaded so you can poke around instead of staring at an empty screen.

Everything here is a real Advisor Prep Hero surface. The files are real files. The editor is the real editor. The AI sidebar talks to a real model.

## What to try

1. Open `Thornwood Landscaping LLC/Client Research Note.md` to see how a CPA researches a tricky deduction question inside Advisor Prep Hero.
2. Open `Thornwood Landscaping LLC/Section 280A Analysis.aichat` to watch a saved AI conversation about the home-office limitation rules.
3. Open `Thornwood Landscaping LLC/Pre-Review Checklist.md` to see a template-style checklist that travels with the workspace.
4. Open the AI sidebar and ask it something about the open file.

On your own machine, these files live in a folder you pick, and your API key goes straight from your computer to the model. Client SSNs, returns, and financial statements never route through a server you do not control. That's the reason a CPA can use Advisor Prep Hero on a live client matter.

Refresh the page and the workspace comes back to where it started.

# Client Research Note: Home-Office Deduction

**Client:** Thornwood Landscaping LLC (sole member: Dale Thornwood)
**Tax year:** 2025
**Prepared by:** [CPA initials]
**Date:** June 2, 2026

## Client question

Dale uses a dedicated room in his home exclusively as the principal place of business for Thornwood. He wants to know whether the LLC can deduct the home-office expenses, how large the deduction is, and whether the Section 280A limitation bites him this year given the LLC had a soft Q4.

## Entity structure note

Thornwood Landscaping LLC is a single-member LLC disregarded for federal income tax purposes. All items flow to Dale's Schedule C on Form 1040. The home-office deduction analysis runs under Section 280A as applied to a sole proprietor, not under the employee home-office rules (suspended post-TCJA through 2025).

## Section 280A: the basic rule

IRC Section 280A(a) disallows deductions for the use of a dwelling unit used as a residence by the taxpayer. The exception at Section 280A(c)(1)(A) allows deductions for a portion of the home used exclusively and on a regular basis as the principal place of business for any trade or business of the taxpayer.

**Exclusively:** the room must be used only for business. A guest bed in the corner defeats the deduction.

**Principal place of business:** the Supreme Court in *Commissioner v. Soliman*, 506 U.S. 168 (1993) established a two-factor test: (1) the relative importance of activities performed at each location; (2) time spent at each location. For a solo landscaping business where administrative and management work is done in the home office and client-facing work is done at job sites, the IRS has consistently treated the home office as the principal place of business if no other fixed location exists for administrative work.

## The 280A(c)(5) gross income limitation

The deduction is limited to the gross income derived from the business use of the home, reduced by:
1. Business expenses allocable to the home that are deductible regardless of business use (mortgage interest, real estate taxes).
2. Business deductions allocable to the home that are not limited by gross income (e.g., depreciation is deferred, not disallowed).

Any disallowed amount carries forward to the next tax year.

## Preliminary numbers (need to confirm with Dale)

| Item | Amount | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Gross income from Schedule C | $148,200 | Need Q4 actuals from QuickBooks |
| Allocable mortgage interest | $3,400 | 12.5% of home, room is 180 sq ft of 1,440 sq ft total |
| Allocable real estate taxes | $820 | Same allocation percentage |
| Other allocable home expenses | $2,100 | Utilities, insurance, repairs at 12.5% |
| Depreciation (allocable) | $1,640 | Cost basis $262,400, 39-year SL, 12.5% allocation |

Preliminary deduction before limitation: ~$7,960. Gross income is well above this, so the 280A(c)(5) limitation should not bite in 2025 even with the soft Q4. Confirm final Schedule C income before filing.

## Open items

- Confirm Q4 revenue figure from Dale's QuickBooks export.
- Confirm room square footage (Dale said "about 180 square feet"; get a measurement).
- Confirm no other business use of the room (Dale mentioned his daughter sometimes does homework there; get the facts).
- Depreciation basis: confirm cost allocable to dwelling (exclude land value).

# Pre-Review Checklist: Thornwood Landscaping LLC / Dale Thornwood

**Tax year:** 2025
**Return type:** Form 1040 with Schedule C
**Reviewer:** [CPA initials]
**Date of review:**

This checklist is a template. Fill in the status column and note any open items before the return goes to the client for signature.

## Identity and entity

- [ ] SSN confirmed against prior-year return
- [ ] Entity classification confirmed: single-member LLC, disregarded entity
- [ ] No new ownership changes during 2025

## Schedule C income

- [ ] Gross receipts reconciled to QuickBooks year-end P&L
- [ ] 1099-NEC received from each payer over $600; all reported
- [ ] No income excluded without documentation

## Home office deduction (Section 280A)

- [ ] Exclusive use confirmed with client (written representation on file)
- [ ] Room square footage confirmed (measurement, not estimate)
- [ ] Total home square footage confirmed
- [ ] Allocation percentage calculated and documented
- [ ] Mortgage interest: 1098 received, allocable amount calculated
- [ ] Real estate taxes: confirmed from county records or 1098
- [ ] Utilities and insurance: receipts on file
- [ ] Depreciation: basis confirmed, prior depreciation schedule reviewed
- [ ] 280A(c)(5) limitation tested against final Schedule C gross income
- [ ] Any carryforward from prior year applied

## Vehicle and mileage

- [ ] Mileage log reviewed (or contemporaneous records confirmed)
- [ ] Business vs. personal split documented
- [ ] Standard mileage or actual expense method consistent with prior years

## Other deductions

- [ ] Equipment purchases: Section 179 election decision made
- [ ] Subcontractor payments: 1099-NEC filings confirmed if required
- [ ] Insurance premiums: self-employed health insurance deduction checked

## Estimated taxes

- [ ] 2025 quarterly payments confirmed against IRS records
- [ ] 2026 estimated payment schedule discussed with client

## Final steps

- [ ] Return reviewed by second CPA or self-review checklist complete
- [ ] Client engagement letter on file for 2025
- [ ] Signed Form 8879 or equivalent obtained before e-file
- [ ] Acknowledgment received after e-file; retained in client folder

**Open items before filing:**

(List any unresolved items here before the return is transmitted.)

# About this demo

This is the in-browser version of Advisor Prep Hero, pre-loaded with a fictional CPA client matter so you have something real to look at.

The client, the names, and the numbers are all made up for illustration. Nothing here is tax advice, and the AI's job in the real app is to produce a first draft or analysis you review, not to practice accounting.

What's different from the real app: this demo uses a shared, rate-limited key so you can try the AI without setting anything up. On your own machine you bring your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or a local model through Ollama). Your files and your key never leave your computer. Your client's SSN and return data never touch a server you do not control.

When you're ready, download the 30-day trial at advisorprephero.com.
